clue.text: Youth with no head for multiplication

definitions.note: a noun here; the answer is the verbal noun for multiplying by three

indicators.note: having no head means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a stripling is a youth, a lad not yet fully grown

explanation.surface: A young pupil who just cannot get the hang of his times tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head' removes the S from STRIPLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Increasing something threefold is a particular kind of multiplication.

clue.text: Here most trouble is made for convalescents

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the place serves; the answer is a place for them

indicators.note: making trouble stirs things up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Patients recovering at a clinic cause the most trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution caring for people recovering from illness or for the elderly.

clue.text: Nearest point at sea for the launch

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship is launched from the nearest point on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A product launch is its formal unveiling to the public.

clue.text: Colour I associate with wrong-doing

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so these letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone links a certain colour with sinful behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong-doing' reads as one word for sin, but splits: 'wrong' is the anagram signal acting on 'doing', with 'associate with' a mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue-violet hue lying between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Criminal group go north of the border

explanation.definitionFit: A band of crooks, and the Scots verb meaning to walk or go; north of the border is Scotland.

clue.text: Immediately cancel, but only verbally

indicators.note: verbally means in speech, so the phrase for cancel is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: to write off a debt is to cancel it

explanation.surface: Someone cancels at once, though only by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means straight away or at once, without delay.

clue.text: Empty honour for a woodwind player

annotationWithheld.why: Empty honour for a woodwind player: OBOE is OBE (honour) with O inside, but 'Empty' must both supply the O and signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Empty honour for a woodwind player

clue.text: A bright little pupil?

parts.note: reads as a clever young schoolchild, but describes a small shining eye whose pupil glints

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a keen, watchful gaze, from small round shining eyes.

clue.text: Cordial or strong mineral accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: able in the sense of able-bodied, robust
mica is a mineral that splits into thin sheets

explanation.surface: Choosing between a fruit cordial and a strong mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like a drink beside 'mineral' water, but it is the adjective meaning friendly; 'accepted' signals one piece taken inside the other, and 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe friendly, warm and good-natured dealings between people.

clue.text: Key heading is missing from passage

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which goes missing here

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A document lacks its title, so the passage reads oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is not a door key but a low island, as in the Florida Keys; 'heading is missing from' drops the A of AISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A key or cay is a small low island, and an isle is a small island.

clue.text: Sounds the way to evade duty?

definitions.text: Sounds the way to evade duty?

parts.words: Sounds the way to evade duty?
parts.note: a sailor taking soundings swings a lead weight on a line; the same phrase is slang for idling or faking illness to dodge work

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shirking work, originally from sailors dodging tasks by slowly heaving the sounding line.

clue.text: It helps when you don't speak the same language

definitions.text: It helps when you don't speak the same language

parts.words: It helps when you don't speak the same language
parts.note: describes a shared tongue adopted by speakers of different native languages

explanation.definitionFit: A common tongue used for communication between groups with different mother tongues.

clue.text: Leaving as a result of being fired

definitions.text: as a result of being fired

explanation.definitionFit: Departing is setting off, and a gun discharges or explodes when fired.

clue.text: Can an obese man have such an attraction?

definitions.note: points to the adjective in the film title Fatal Attraction

parts.note: fat means very overweight
Al is a common man's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a very heavy man can be so irresistible.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls up the 1987 thriller Fatal Attraction; 'Can' and 'have' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly is the adjective in the phrase for a dangerous, destructive infatuation.

clue.text: Fancy becoming a tenor maybe

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so these letters change shape

parts.note: the words a tenor supply the letters; maybe just softens the surface, a tenor perhaps being any singer

explanation.surface: Someone imagines turning into a tenor, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning imagine, but it is the adjective; 'becoming' signals that the letters of A TENOR turn into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy decoration is elaborate and showy, the same as highly decorated.

clue.text: Hear about the wife of Zeus

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Learning about the wife of the king of the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the queen of the gods was married to Zeus, king of Olympus.

clue.text: It's difficult to reproduce in printed form

parts.note: hard means difficult
to copy is to reproduce or duplicate

explanation.surface: Something tricky to duplicate on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing term for a document on paper rather than on screen.

clue.text: It's an idea to return healthy to the doctor

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a standard abbreviation for an army doctor

indicators.note: to return means the word for healthy goes back the way it came

parts.note: fit means in good health

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a recovered patient go back to the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (Medical Officer) is a long-standing crossword abbreviation for a doctor; 'to return' reverses the word for healthy, and 'It's an' is padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring theme or central concept in a work of art.

clue.text: Mother joins other females making complaints

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
ladies are women, females other than the mother

explanation.surface: Mum joins the other women, all of them grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' looks like grumbles, but means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment or disorder, like a stomach complaint.

clue.text: Surgeon's inner compulsion

indicators.note: inner points to letters found inside the surgeon's word

explanation.surface: A surgeon feels a deep inner drive to operate.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire, a pressing drive to act.

clue.text: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?

definitions.text: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?

parts.words: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?
parts.note: a warm benevolent feeling, and also what heirs might feel about a generous testament

explanation.definitionFit: Friendly benevolence, and punningly a favourable testament left to heirs.

clue.text: Type of tyre having spokes?

explanation.definitionFit: A radial-ply tyre has cords running across it, and spokes radiate from a wheel's hub.

clue.text: A golfer upset about pro's first game

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the other piece
upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are scrambled
first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A golfer gets upset over a professional's first round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' sits at the end as the definition; 'upset' scrambles A GOLFER, and 'about' wraps that scramble round the 'first' letter of pro's.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Corrupt practices a sailor employs

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
uses means employs

explanation.surface: A dishonest sailor is caught out by his crooked dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or wrongful practices, as in abuses of power.

clue.text: Bram stoker's batman

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote a famous Gothic novel whose title vampire can turn into a bat

explanation.walkthrough: A batman is an officer's servant, but here it is a man who becomes a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Transylvanian vampire nobleman of Stoker's 1897 novel can transform into a bat.

clue.text: Initially, they're thought by some to come from outer space

definitions.text: Initially, they're thought by some to come from outer space

parts.words: Initially, they're thought by some to come from outer space
parts.note: 'Initially' says the answer is a set of initials, for flying objects some believe are alien craft

explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects, which some people believe are alien spacecraft.

clue.text: Highly placed at work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.definitionFit: On top of something, set high above it.

clue.text: Innocent abroad?

parts.note: the French word for simple and unworldly, borrowed into English

explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for naive and artless, so a foreign way of saying innocent.

clue.text: Shakespearian character to thrive on love?

parts.note: to prosper is to thrive or flourish
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Shakespeare figure would flourish on love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just means one piece follows the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The exiled magician duke in The Tempest is one of Shakespeare's characters.

clue.text: Fair examinations should be!

explanation.definitionFit: A fair piece of work is adequate, and an exam should be possible to get through.
